sentences.text: Shri Mohammed Anas Sheikh - Advocate for the objector/respondent No.2.
Heard o n I.A. No. 15982/2023, which is first application filed under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of the appellant - Magan S/o Bherulal.
Notice has been served to the victim and State has filed the reply.
In the reply it is stated that the father of the victim has filed "No Objection" alongwith an Affidavit and Adhar Card wherein stating that they have compromised the matter.

Learned Trial Court has convicted the appellant under Sections 363 of IPC, 376 (3) of IPC and Sec 5 L/6 of POCSO Act and 366 of IPC and 506 Part - II of IPC and sentenced him to undergo RI for 3 years with fine of Rs.500/-, RI for 20 years with fine of Rs.10,000, RI for 3 years with fine of Rs.500/- and 6 months RI respectively with default stipulations, vide judgement of conviction and order of sentence dated 17.04.2023 passed by the Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012) Petlawad,
District Jhabua in S.T. No.08/2021.
Prosecution story found to be proved is that on 04.03.2021, the father of the prosecutrix lodged a report at Chowki Sarangi that after dinner on 08.02.2021 all his family member went to sleep.

entities.text:
Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012) Petlawad,
District Jhabua
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On next morning i.e. on 09.02.2021 around 6 - 7 AM when he called her daughter to prepare tea for him there was no response from the room and as soon as he went inside the room to look after her daughter she was not found in the room.

Inquiry was done from his neighbor and relatives, but she was not traced out and on the basis of doubt that the appellant Magan might abducted her daughter by amusing her lodged a report against the appellant.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant has not committed any offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.

sentences.text: was marked.

The trial Court itself discussed and found that no document was produced and the Headmaster of the school has stated before the Court that in the concerned area, children aged between 6-7 are got admitted in the school and the date of birth is entered on the basis of prediction and at the time of admission of the victim at school, no relevant document was filed by the parents of the victim and the father of the victim has himself admitted that he has not submitted any document at School when her daughter was got admitted in the School.
Learned counsel for the appellant has further argued that FIR was lodged after one month.
The victim was the consenting party .
At the time of incident the appellant was aged about 19 years and he has no criminal past track record.
He is a permanent resident of Jhabua and there is no chance of absconding.

Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future since the appeal is of the year 2023, therefore, it is prayed that the remaining sentence may be suspended and the appellant may be released on bail.

Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State as well as the learned counsel for the Objector has opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and submitted that the appellant is not the consenting party and she was minor during the time of incident.
Moreso, appellant has not suffered considerable period of custody.
Hence, the application for suspension deserves to be dismissed.
We have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

Looking to the fact and circumstances of the case and taking into account the age of the appellant and keeping in mind that the final hearing of this appeal shall take a long time, the application I.A.
No. 15982/2023, is allowed and the jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended.

I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if already not deposited, appellant shall be released on bail, on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) along with solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court firstly on 29.07.2024, and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
C.C. as per rules.
